messages:
support: FYI customer AcmeCorp reports p99 spike ~20-30s starting ~08:12 UTC, saw auth failures and billing 429s mixed in. stack: continuous-batcher path. anyone oncall?
sam: I see the alert, jumping in. which fleet/region?
support: us-west-2 inference-prod pool-3. Correlated with a commit rolled 08:05 that adjusted batching hold windows and auth refresh backoff.
maria: can you paste the relevant logs?
support: pasted snippets below 
```
[08:12:18 UTC] request_id=abc123 status=200 latency_ms=1300 batch_size=1 -> normal
[08:12:18 UTC] request_id=abc124 status=200 latency_ms=21000 batch_size=1 auth_error=token_refresh_failed
[08:12:19 UTC] request_id=abc125 status=429 latency_ms=5 batch_size=1 billing_rate_limit=true
[08:12:20 UTC] request_id=abc126 status=200 latency_ms=24000 batch_size=2 coalesce_delay_ms=0
```
support: also saw many tiny batches (batch_size 1-2) during the window.
elaine: that log combo looks like two things: token refresh flapping -> requests bypass coalescer, and billing 429s triggering retries that hammer small batches.
sam: good catch. which deploy changed coalescing? I have the PR: `eg/runner: reduce max_hold_ms for tiny-requests` rolled 08:05.
maria: show config used in canary please
support: config applied in pool-3 canary: 
```
continuous_batcher: 
  grace_window_ms: 8
  hold_ms: 4
  max_batch_size: 8
  prefer_latency_over_throughput: true
```
ops-oncall: That hold_ms of 4 + grace_window 8 is very aggressive for tiny prompts. If auth refresh causes one request to stall, others are flushed immediately -> tiny batches and tail.
sam: aha. Also PR relaxed auth backoff, we now try immediate token refresh once per request, failing ones get auth_error and cause immediate fallback path.
maria: so two levers: batching hold/grace and auth refresh behavior + billing retry logic. Need repro steps.
support: repro: run loadgen with many short prompts (10-20 tokens) at QPS 120-180, with simulated token refresh latency 50-200ms on 1% of requests, and inject billing-limit responses (HTTP 429) at 0.5% bursts. Observed p99 > 15s within 3-4 minutes.
sam: can you post the minimal harness command?
support: `./loadgen --qps 150 --prompt-size 12 --token-refresh-fail-rate 0.01 --billing-burst 0.005 --duration 600`
elaine: thanks. mitigation options: 1) rollback hold_ms to previous (12ms) and set grace_window 20ms, 2) change auth refresh to use centralized refresh (dedupe) so it doesn't block main path, 3) add early-batch aggregation to tolerate auth delays.
maria: immediate next step: rollback the canary config and re-run load test. I'll take rollback.
sam: I can patch auth refresh dedupe as a short-term toggle (feature flag).
ops-oncall: also throttle client-side retry for 429s to exponential backoff instead of immediate retry -> reduces small-batch pressure.
support: customer impact note: AcmeCorp seeing degraded UX, opened P0 case. We should notify CS after fix deployed.
maria: rolling back now to previous config (applied to pool-3). command: `deployctl set-config pool-3 continuous_batcher.hold_ms=12 continuous_batcher.grace_window_ms=20`
sre-bot: deploy event: config-change accepted by orchestrator, rollout started to pool-3 canary nodes (5/50)
sam: I'll enable auth-dedupe flag on canary only after rollback finishes.
maria: rollback finished to canary nodes at 08:23, metrics already showing batch_size median rising to 6 and p99 trending down.
support: customer confirmed improvement, p99 dropped to ~1.1s after rollback.
elaine: let's create a followup ticket: ACTIONS: (a) revert PR that reduced hold to aggressive numbers until auth dedupe in place, (b) add automated load test that simulates intermittent token refresh failures, (c) implement 429 client backoff change.
sam: creating ticket INF-3482 and assigning to eng-runtime (me), eng-auth (maria), and eng-sre (elaine).
maria: I'll own the auth dedupe flag patch and canary it tomorrow.
ops-oncall: I'll update runbook to note this auth+billing interaction for tiny prompts.
support: closing loop with AcmeCorp and CS notified. Thanks all :thumbsup:
sre-bot: incident-note: p99-latency spike caused by aggressive coalesce/hold reduction combined with token-refresh failures and billing retry bursts. Mitigated by rollback of batching config.
